title: N-ary Tree Level Order Traversal
spaceBreakdown:
- queue<Node*> q: holds up to the widest level, at most n nodes → O(n)
- vector<int> level per iteration: reused, max width O(n) → O(n) transient
- result vector: returned output, not counted
- recursion depth: none (iterative)
approach: Use breadth-first search: push the root into a queue, then repeatedly process the entire current queue size as one level - popping those nodes, collecting their values, and enqueuing all their children. Capturing `q.size()` before the inner loop guarantees each output sublist contains exactly one depth level. This visits every node once, so it is optimal for the 10^4-node limit.
hints: What single property is shared by every node that ends up in the same output sublist? The tree can hold up to 10^4 nodes.
Use a FIFO queue (BFS). On Example 1, start with queue = [1]; pop 1, record [1], enqueue its children 3,2,4 - those three form the next sublist.

```
if root is null: return empty
queue = [root]
while queue not empty:
    sz = queue.size()
    level = []
    repeat sz times:
        node = queue.pop_front()
        level.append(node.val)
        for child in node.children:
            queue.push_back(child)
    result.append(level)
return result
```

**Empty tree** - root is null
`Input: []` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: dereferencing `root->val` before a null check → runtime error

**Single node** - root has no children
`Input: [1]` → `Expected: [[1]]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping `result.push_back(level)` when `node->children` is empty → returns `[]`

**Not snapshotting queue size** - using `q.size()` inside the loop condition
`Input: [1,null,3,2,4,null,5,6]` → `Expected: [[1],[3,2,4],[5,6]]`
⚠️ Bug: writing `for (int i=0; i<q.size(); i++)` and pushing children inside → returns `[[1,3,2,4,5,6]]`

**Skewed tree** - each node has one child, height 1000
`Input: [1,null,2,null,3,null,...]` → `Expected: [[1],[2],[3],...]`
⚠️ Bug: recursive DFS collecting by depth → stack overflow at depth 1000

followUps.q: Return the level order traversal bottom-up (last level first).
followUps.a: Run the same BFS, then reverse the result vector before returning. Time stays O(n), space O(n).

followUps.q: Return a zigzag level order: left-to-right on even levels, right-to-left on odd levels.
followUps.a: Keep the BFS, but reverse each level vector when the level index is odd before appending. Time O(n), space O(n).

followUps.q: Nodes arrive as a stream of child iterators and the full tree does not fit in memory.
followUps.a: Use iterative-deepening DFS with depth limit d = 0, 1, 2, …; each pass emits one level without storing the whole tree. Time O(n·h), space O(h) for the recursion stack.
